audit_status.source_base: Greek Romans text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for baptism into death/life, old human, sin as enslaving power, grace not permission, slavery metaphor, wages/gift.

verses.restored: What then shall we say? Should we remain in sin/misalignment so that grace may abound?

familiar.text: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?

modern.text: What then shall we say? Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase?

original.text: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; ⸀ἐπιμένωμεν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, ἵνα ἡ χάρις πλεονάσῃ;

verses.restored: May it not be. We who died to sin/misalignment, how shall we still live in it?

familiar.text: God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?

modern.text: Certainly not! How can we who died to sin live in it any longer?

original.text: μὴ γένοιτο· οἵτινες ἀπεθάνομεν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, πῶς ἔτι ζήσομεν ἐν αὐτῇ;

verses.restored: Or do you not know that as many of us as were baptized into Messiah Jesus were baptized into his death?

familiar.text: Know ye not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death?

modern.text: Or aren’t you aware that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?

original.text: ἢ ἀγνοεῖτε ὅτι ὅσοι ἐβαπτίσθημεν εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν εἰς τὸν θάνατον αὐτοῦ ἐβαπτίσθημεν;

verses.restored: Therefore we were buried together with him through baptism into death, so that just as Messiah was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life.

familiar.text: Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life.

modern.text: We were therefore buried with Him through baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may walk in newness of life.

original.text: συνετάφημεν οὖν αὐτῷ διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος εἰς τὸν θάνατον, ἵνα ὥσπερ ἠγέρθη Χριστὸς ἐκ νεκρῶν διὰ τῆς δόξης τοῦ πατρός, οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐν καινότητι ζωῆς περιπατήσωμεν.

verses.restored: For if we have become united with the likeness of his death, certainly we will also be of the resurrection.

familiar.text: For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection:

modern.text: For if we have been united with Him like this in His death, we will certainly also be united with Him in His resurrection.

original.text: Εἰ γὰρ σύμφυτοι γεγόναμεν τῷ ὁμοιώματι τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἐσόμεθα·

verses.restored: Knowing this, that our old human was crucified together, so that the body of sin/misalignment might be made inactive, that we no longer be enslaved to sin/misalignment.

familiar.text: Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin.

modern.text: We know that our old self was crucified with Him so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless, that we should no longer be slaves to sin.

original.text: τοῦτο γινώσκοντες ὅτι ὁ παλαιὸς ἡμῶν ἄνθρωπος συνεσταυρώθη, ἵνα καταργηθῇ τὸ σῶμα τῆς ἁμαρτίας, τοῦ μηκέτι δουλεύειν ἡμᾶς τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ,

verses.restored: For the one who died has been made righteous/just away from sin/misalignment.

familiar.text: For he that is dead is freed from sin.

modern.text: For anyone who has died has been freed from sin.

original.text: ὁ γὰρ ἀποθανὼν δεδικαίωται ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας.

verses.restored: If we died with Messiah, we trust that we will also live with him,

familiar.text: Now if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him:

modern.text: Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with Him.

original.text: εἰ δὲ ἀπεθάνομεν σὺν Χριστῷ, πιστεύομεν ὅτι καὶ συζήσομεν αὐτῷ·

verses.restored: knowing that Messiah, having been raised from the dead, dies no more; death no longer rules over him.

familiar.text: Knowing that Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death hath no more dominion over him.

modern.text: For we know that since Christ was raised from the dead, He cannot die again; death no longer has dominion over Him.

original.text: εἰδότες ὅτι Χριστὸς ἐγερθεὶς ἐκ νεκρῶν οὐκέτι ἀποθνῄσκει, θάνατος αὐτοῦ οὐκέτι κυριεύει·

verses.restored: For the death he died, he died to sin/misalignment once for all; but the life he lives, he lives to the Divine.

familiar.text: For in that he died, he died unto sin once: but in that he liveth, he liveth unto God.

modern.text: The death He died, He died to sin once for all; but the life He lives, He lives to God.

original.text: ὃ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν, τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἀπέθανεν ἐφάπαξ· ὃ δὲ ζῇ, ζῇ τῷ θεῷ.

verses.restored: So also you, calculate yourselves dead indeed to sin/misalignment, but alive to the Divine in Messiah Jesus.

familiar.text: Likewise reckon ye also yourselves to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord.

modern.text: So you too must count yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.

original.text: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς λογίζεσθε ἑαυτοὺς ⸂εἶναι νεκροὺς μὲν⸃ τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ζῶντας δὲ τῷ θεῷ ἐν Χριστῷ ⸀Ἰησοῦ.

verses.restored: Therefore do not let sin/misalignment reign in your mortal body, to obey its desires.

familiar.text: Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.

modern.text: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body so that you obey its desires.

original.text: Μὴ οὖν βασιλευέτω ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θνητῷ ὑμῶν σώματι εἰς τὸ ⸀ὑπακούειν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις αὐτοῦ,

verses.restored: Do not present your members to sin/misalignment as instruments of injustice, but present yourselves to the Divine as those alive from the dead, and your members to the Divine as instruments of righteousness/justice.

familiar.text: Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.

modern.text: Do not present the parts of your body to sin as instruments of wickedness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life; and present the parts of your body to Him as instruments of righteousness.

original.text: μηδὲ παριστάνετε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν ὅπλα ἀδικίας τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, ἀλλὰ παραστήσατε ἑαυτοὺς τῷ θεῷ ⸀ὡσεὶ ἐκ νεκρῶν ζῶντας καὶ τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν ὅπλα δικαιοσύνης τῷ θεῷ.

verses.restored: For sin/misalignment will not rule over you, for you are not under Law but under grace.

familiar.text: For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.

modern.text: For sin shall not be your master, because you are not under law, but under grace. The Wages of Sin

original.text: ἁμαρτία γὰρ ὑμῶν οὐ κυριεύσει, οὐ γάρ ἐστε ὑπὸ νόμον ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ χάριν.

verses.restored: What then? Should we sin/misalign because we are not under Law but under grace? May it not be.

familiar.text: What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid.

modern.text: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law, but under grace? Certainly not!

original.text: Τί οὖν; ⸀ἁμαρτήσωμεν ὅτι οὐκ ἐσμὲν ὑπὸ νόμον ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ χάριν; μὴ γένοιτο·

verses.restored: Do you not know that to whom you present yourselves as enslaved ones for obedience, you are enslaved to the one you obey, whether sin/misalignment into death or obedience into righteousness/justice?

familiar.text: Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?

modern.text: Do you not know that when you offer yourselves as obedient slaves, you are slaves to the one you obey, whether you are slaves to sin leading to death, or to obedience leading to righteousness?

original.text: οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ᾧ παριστάνετε ἑαυτοὺς δούλους εἰς ὑπακοήν, δοῦλοί ἐστε ᾧ ὑπακούετε, ἤτοι ἁμαρτίας εἰς θάνατον ἢ ὑπακοῆς εἰς δικαιοσύνην;

verses.restored: But thanks to the Divine, that though you were enslaved to sin/misalignment, you obeyed from the heart the pattern of teaching to which you were handed over,

familiar.text: But God be thanked, that ye were the servants of sin, but ye have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you.

modern.text: But thanks be to God that, though you once were slaves to sin, you wholeheartedly obeyed the form of teaching to which you were committed.

original.text: χάρις δὲ τῷ θεῷ ὅτι ἦτε δοῦλοι τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὑπηκούσατε δὲ ἐκ καρδίας εἰς ὃν παρεδόθητε τύπον διδαχῆς,

verses.restored: and having been released from sin/misalignment, you were enslaved to righteousness/justice.

familiar.text: Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness.

modern.text: You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness.

original.text: ἐλευθερωθέντες δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἐδουλώθητε τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ·

verses.restored: I speak in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. For just as you presented your members enslaved to uncleanness and lawlessness into lawlessness, so now present your members enslaved to righteousness/justice into sanctification.

familiar.text: I speak after the manner of men because of the infirmity of your flesh: for as ye have yielded your members servants to uncleanness and to iniquity unto iniquity; even so now yield your members servants to righteousness unto holiness.

modern.text: I am speaking in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. Just as you used to offer the parts of your body in slavery to impurity and to escalating wickedness, so now offer them in slavery to righteousness leading to holiness.

original.text: ἀνθρώπινον λέγω διὰ τὴν ἀσθένειαν τῆς σαρκὸς ὑμῶν· ὥσπερ γὰρ παρεστήσατε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν δοῦλα τῇ ἀκαθαρσίᾳ καὶ τῇ ἀνομίᾳ εἰς τὴν ἀνομίαν, οὕτως νῦν παραστήσατε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν δοῦλα τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ εἰς ἁγιασμόν.

verses.restored: For when you were enslaved to sin/misalignment, you were free with respect to righteousness/justice.

familiar.text: For when ye were the servants of sin, ye were free from righteousness.

modern.text: For when you were slaves to sin, you were free of obligation to righteousness.

original.text: Ὅτε γὰρ δοῦλοι ἦτε τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ἐλεύθεροι ἦτε τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ.

verses.restored: What fruit then did you have at that time, of which you are now ashamed? For the completion of those things is death.

familiar.text: What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death.

modern.text: What fruit did you reap at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? The outcome of those things is death.

original.text: τίνα οὖν καρπὸν εἴχετε τότε ἐφʼ οἷς νῦν ἐπαισχύνεσθε; τὸ γὰρ τέλος ἐκείνων θάνατος·

verses.restored: But now, having been released from sin/misalignment and enslaved to the Divine, you have your fruit into sanctification, and the completion age-long life.

familiar.text: But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life.

modern.text: But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves to God, the fruit you reap leads to holiness, and the outcome is eternal life.

original.text: νυνὶ δέ, ἐλευθερωθέντες ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας δουλωθέντες δὲ τῷ θεῷ, ἔχετε τὸν καρπὸν ὑμῶν εἰς ἁγιασμόν, τὸ δὲ τέλος ζωὴν αἰώνιον.

verses.restored: For the wages of sin/misalignment is death, but the gift of the Divine is age-long life in Messiah Jesus our Lord.

familiar.text: For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

modern.text: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

original.text: τὰ γὰρ ὀψώνια τῆς ἁμαρτίας θάνατος, τὸ δὲ χάρισμα τοῦ θεοῦ ζωὴ αἰώνιος ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν.

translation_notes: Romans 6 uses slavery imagery as a moral-political metaphor of belonging and obedience. It should be handled carefully and not romanticized.
Under grace is not permission to misalign; Paul frames grace as liberation from the rule of sin/death into embodied justice.
